_comment: Every scheduled run writes one record here — including, especially, a run that could not connect. A failed run that logs is data; a failed run that stays silent is a hole in the record, and a hole is indistinguishable from a run that never fired. Record shape: { date, slot: open|hourly|preclose|retro, at, fired, connected, actions, note }. 'connected' means the brokerage connector attached and the run read live account state; a run that reasoned only from this repo's JSON is fired=true, connected=false. Per-run rows begin on recordsBeginOn. Anything earlier is carried in priorSummary as an aggregate, because those runs predate this file and the per-run detail was never written down. Do not backfill it.

scheduler.note: True as of 2026-08-05, and read it narrowly. This is a desktop scheduled task, not a server-side runner — it fires only while the operator's Claude app is open, so a missed window runs late on next launch rather than on time. Every run therefore checks how late it fired and refuses to write an order specification if the quotes it would rest on are stale. On 2026-08-05 all nine rows fired inside their own windows, four to seven minutes late, so the guard was never the thing that stopped a run — but one clean day is one clean day, not a server. The example this note used to cite, a retro slot of 16:30 ET firing at 00:45 ET, was removed with the test rows on 8/5 and is described here rather than pointed at, because the file no longer contains it. 'Configured' means a trigger exists and has fired, not that the four slots fire reliably at their stated times.

slots.name: Market open
slots.does: Verify the connector attached before reasoning about anything. Check settled cash, apply exit rules, run the six-item pre-trade checklist.

slots.name: Mid-session
slots.does: Enforce exits the hour a level is hit. Default is no trade.

slots.name: Pre-close
slots.does: Exit discipline. Decide overnight holds explicitly rather than by default. Close option no-fly windows.

slots.name: Retro
slots.does: Read-only. Grades the day against the rules outcome-blind, then runs the standing rule-drift check. Never places an order.

First retro to fire in its own window: 16:33 ET against the 16:30 slot, three minutes late, and grading a session that has already settled so lateness costs it nothing. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly. Read-only throughout, as this slot always is. The headline finding is that the board was wrong when the session ended: the account is FLAT. The 4 UPST were sold at 30.3801 at 15:38:23 ET, 84 seconds after the pre-close run read the book and decided to hold, and about two and a half minutes before that run pushed 'Holding 4 UPST overnight' to the live site. Both UPST legs reconciled against the API - bought 31.0899 at 13:34:59, sold 30.3801 at 15:38:23, no fees, P/L -2.84 at -2.28% over 2h 03m - and the broker's own realized-P/L endpoint returns the same -2.84 on one closing trade. Account total 126.06, being 4.54 settled and 121.52 unsettled until 8/6. Both legs are filed 'directed', not 'agent': the broker reports placed_agent='agentic' on each, but why.json contains no order specification standing behind either, and with no specification there is no path to the autonomy column. agentTrades stays 0. Neither fill has any reasoning entry at all, which is recorded in the ledger as a gap rather than papered over with a 'did' entry the runs never wrote. Eight 8/5 entries graded, all outcome-blind: seven PASS, and the pre-close PASS on its reasoning with a flag for publishing a hold that was already false at push time. Both mandate arms are legitimately empty - no specification has been published under the daily entry mandate yet, and the mandate landed at 11:34 ET, after that day's open run had fired, so 8/6 is the first open slot it binds. No bench row written: the official settled closes for SPY, QQQ and SMH were still unpublished at 16:37 ET and a last-trade print is not an official close. state.json and moves.json are stale on the closed position and belong to the trading runs, so they are flagged in the ledger rather than edited here.

Fired 09:41 ET against the 09:33 slot, eight minutes late, inside the 25-minute staleness guard in both directions. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly. The retro was right and the board was wrong: the account is flat. No equity positions, no option positions, and the 121.52 that was unsettled overnight has settled T+1, so deployable is the whole 126.06 rather than the 4.54 state.json still carried. No exit was due because there is nothing to exit. First specification published under the daily entry mandate, and it is FORCED on item 1: buy 12 SMR at a 9.75 limit, target 11.70, stop 8.97, time stop the 8/13 close. SMR reported 8/5 after the close at -0.13 against a -0.13 estimate - exactly in line - and an in-line EPS is not an answer to 'why does this move meaningfully, soon'. I can read the print but not the driver, so naming a catalyst here would mean inferring one from the price, which is the thing item 1 exists to stop. Items 2, 4, 5 and 6 pass and item 3 is na. It is the pick because of item 5: of the four names that printed last night, SMR is the only one being bought. It opened 9.30, below its own 9.38 close, flushed to 9.19 and has made three consecutive higher closes through the 8/5 high on accelerating volume. SOUN gapped +25% and is -4.3% from its open on 11M shares in fifteen minutes, IONQ has given back 1.8% of a 45% EPS beat, JOBY faded off 8.20 on three declining-volume bars. Options were checked before the thesis, as the rulebook now requires, and rejected again - but on spread, not affordability, which is new: at 126.06 the account can finally pay for a contract, and the JOBY 9/11 $8.00 call at a 0.85 mark still quotes 0.72/0.98, 30.6% of mark against a 10% ceiling.

_rowFields: trigger: 'scheduled' when the scheduler fired this run in its own window, 'manual' when a human invoked it. Only scheduled rows count toward run health - a manual invocation proves the code path works, not that the system runs. declined: true when the run deliberately stopped on a guard (fired outside its window, or the mandate was unset) and therefore never attempted to reach the broker. A decline is correct behaviour, not a connection failure, and it is excluded from the run-health denominator rather than counted against it.
